title: Linode Pricing: Plans, Costs and Extra Fees (2026)
summary: Linode pricing includes flat monthly rates for compute plans. Compare plan costs and estimate your hosting bill for different workload sizes.
body_markdown:
## When hyperscalers beat Linode's pricing


Ask early, because the other side has a real argument: for some buyers, a hyperscaler's discounts, credits and managed services will beat Linode's flat pricing, and you should know which buyers those are before you commit.


### Discounts and reserved pricing elsewhere


AWS and its rivals hand out startup credits, free tiers and commitment discounts. A credit can cover a first year's bill entirely, so a small team may pay nothing while Linode charges from day one.


Reserved and savings plans, where you promise to use a set amount for a year or three in exchange for a lower rate, can cut the instance price well below the listed one.


It shows the gap's large, but a credit hides that gap only while the credit lasts.


When it runs out, **the metered rate's what you pay** .


The same trap shows up in the tools you run on the server, where billing by detail taxes the builder for splitting work into smaller, safer steps.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) charges 1 credit per flow run however many steps it holds, so a ten-step flow costs what the two-step workaround did.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, and on Activepieces the Plus plan is $20 a month for 10,000 credits, so the run is what gets metered.


If your users are mostly in Europe and you only need plain virtual machines, Hetzner wins on the headline number, and you should say so plainly. Hetzner, a German hosting company, lists lower prices than Linode for comparable small servers.


What you give up is a smaller set of regions and add-ons, which matters if your customers sit elsewhere.


### Managed services hyperscalers offer that Linode lacks


Managed databases, identity systems, queues and security tooling are what hyperscalers sell that you'd otherwise build and watch yourself. Doing that work yourself costs staff hours, and a missed patch costs more than a month of hosting.


Akamai, the content delivery and security company that owns Linode, has been widening Linode's managed offering, but the catalog is still thinner.


If your workload leans on those services, the cheaper instance isn't the cheaper bill.
